full_judgment:
A.M. Mahmudur Rahman, J: This revisional application is against the order dated 16.4.84 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge in Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1982 restoring the same to its file and number vacating the order dated 5.12.83 dismissing the case for non-prosecution. 

 2. The aforesaid order was passed upon an application filed under Section 151 of the  Code of Civil Procedure on the ground that the Miscellaneous Case was dismissed on 5.12.83 for non-prosecution on the basis of an application filed by the lawyer of the opposite parties without having been authorised to file such application and the said order was obtained by practicing fraud upon the Court. 

 4. The said Miscellaneous Case was filled for restoration of Title Suit No. 58 of 1980 decreed ex-parte on 30.12.81. The remedy available under section 151 of the Code is, not, so circumscribed in the present case as contended by the learned Advocate. Power given under Section 151 of the Code is available to a Court and it can pass an order in exercise of its inherent power to revise its own order obtained by a party by practice of fraud upon it in order prevent abuse of the process of the Court. But it would be otherwise where it is a case of fraud between the parties and the aggrieved party has a remedy by a separate suit. In this case before me as the opposite parties want to say that the order of dismissal of the Miscellaneous Case No. 22 of 1982 was obtained by practice of fraud upon the Court, the court passing the said order was competent to rectify the wrong by invoking the inherent power under section 151 of the Code of Civil Proceeding. This view of mine finds support from the decision in the case of Abdul Majid Kha-Vs-Mahmudabi reported in 1949 Nag. 366 wherein it has been held that: 

 "The inherent powers may be exercised in a case where the court has been misled by fraud practised upon it because in such a case the court would be under a duty to correct its own proceedings which, in the absence of any other provision, it would do by resort to inherent powers. But when it is a case of fraud between the parties and the aggrieved party has another remedy of a suit open to it, there should be no occasion for invoking inherent powers of the Court". 

 Moreover in this case, if the Miscellaneous Case for restoration of the suit decreed ex-parte is restored and heard the petitioners will not be prejudiced either. 

 5. It also seems to me that the learned Subordinate Judge after perusing the application, hearing the parties and considering the case of the petitioners passed the impugned order. In this view of the matter, I am of the opinion that he was satisfied regarding fraud practised upon him and thus it cannot be said that he has not considered the question of fraud, although he has not come to the finding to the effect in express term. As the impugned order passed on consideration of facts and circumstances of the case and the petitioners will not be prejudiced if the Miscellaneous Case is heard I think that the order complained of has been passed in all fairness to prevent abuse of the process of the Court.
